JSON-3.title: Finite serialization and reconstruction boundaries
JSON-3.body: ### 46.3. JSON-3 — Finite serialization and reconstruction boundaries **Type:** ECOSYSTEM POLICY | **Origin:** USER POLICY | **Applies:** JSON self-reference, generated envelopes, and historical recovery packaging #### 46.3.1. Finite generated-envelope reconstruction The App Plan MUST define a mathematically finite serialization and reconstruction policy. Individual and global JSON representations MUST be reproducible from their defined payload, schema and documented deterministic envelope rules without recursively embedding exact copies of themselves. Define which recovery envelopes are reconstructed, what their byte/semantic reconstruction target is, and preserve any non-derivable retained information they carry. Exact original-file reconstruction under [JSON-1](#json-1) remains mandatory; a serialization boundary cannot discard ordinary retained user content. #### 46.3.2. Retained history and packaging boundaries The current global representation MUST NOT recursively embed itself, unbounded historical snapshots containing themselves, or recursively nested temporary transaction machinery. Distinguish retained user/domain history and necessary recovery information, which remain covered, from separately protected snapshot generations and reconstructible recovery packaging. Document each exclusion's reconstruction or independent retention/access contract, keys/readers and failure limits; exclude only the recursive/generated or genuinely transient packaging, not user data hidden inside it. All still-retained historical user payloads and history/log information belong in the individual/component and global literal coverage inventory; a separate protected generation or history pointer alone does not satisfy that current coverage. A packaging exclusion cannot remove these payloads. Temporary staging is not an ordinary retained original, but any pending user information or operation evidence needed for the declared durable recovery point requires an explicit preservation and reconstruction contract. Historical points themselves MUST have finite, complete declared recovery scopes and accessible dependencies. Reference chains with missing content are not complete recovery payloads. #### 46.3.3. Self-hashes and deterministic serialization Hash domains MUST be explicit and reproducibly verifiable, including how self-generated digest fields and revision identifiers are treated. Do not presume a field can contain the digest of the entire finalized byte string including that same field. Payload-only or explicitly excluded-field domains are examples to evaluate, not a selected universal mechanism. Deterministic envelope serialization must include all necessary version/metadata inputs when exact generated-envelope bytes are promised; semantic reconstruction must be labeled separately. This rule requires coherent finite boundaries and evidence, not a selected universal serialization, staging, commit or history algorithm. Decisions remain under [section 50.2](#open-engineering).

JSON-4.title: Committed revision, distributed state, and verified restoration
JSON-4.body: ### 46.4. JSON-4 — Committed revision, distributed state, and verified restoration **Type:** ECOSYSTEM POLICY | **Origin:** USER POLICY | **Applies:** saving, synchronization, conflict resolution, and restoration of retained-data workspaces #### 46.4.1. Committed revision and legitimate authority The App Plan MUST define how a valid committed revision is established and how originals, individual JSON, global JSON, catalog, and required evidence relate to that revision. Both JSON layers are first-class recovery sources; conflicting copies MUST NOT independently declare incompatible states authoritative. A newer timestamp, matching hash, syntactically valid JSON or equal copies alone does not establish legitimacy, factual correctness or successful commit. Use enforced authority, current-state coordination and validation under [AUTH-1](#auth-1), [CON-1](#con-1), [STORE-1](#store-1), [AUDIT-2](#audit-2) and [OUT-1](#out-1). #### 46.4.2. Continuous checking and evidenced reconciliation Continuous integrity checking and reconciliation MUST have a documented schedule and trust/commit boundaries appropriate to the supported workload. The authorized, tested reconciliation procedure MUST compare relevant current records/revisions, detect mismatches, determine the last verified common state where establishable, examine durable operation evidence, distinguish committed changes from incomplete updates, preserve disputed versions when necessary and lawful, prevent automatic propagation of unvalidated corruption, verify the resulting representations, and record the actual outcome. If common state or legitimacy cannot be established, report uncertainty and preserve safe evidence; do not invent a winner or perform unrestricted mutual overwriting. #### 46.4.3. Pending states and unresolved saving decisions Saving/acknowledgement timing, staging format, write protocol and universal authoritative-copy topology remain unresolved. An App Plan MUST resolve material choices through research and applicable owner authority before affected production implementation under [DEV-5](#dev-5). Do not infer permission either for early pending-state acknowledgement or a universal wait-for-both-copies policy. Honest statuses MUST describe the actual durable recovery point and pending/incomplete/unknown state; no incomplete JSON may masquerade as a complete committed recovery representation. Deferral MUST NOT waive eventual complete individual/global payload obligations or approve hidden fallback storage. #### 46.4.4. Multi-device and storage-provider boundaries For supported laptop, phone, desktop/mobile, NAS, selected cloud or multi-device configurations, define write coordination, working copies, revision IDs, synchronization boundaries, offline operations, conflicts, delayed updates, connection/permission failures, recovery and movement between configurations. Preserve the enabled NAS hub policy under [SYNC-3](#sync-3) without treating it as final universal copy authority. Do not assume a shared physical writable filesystem works everywhere, ordinary cloud-folder sync atomically publishes huge JSON, or independent devices may edit a live SQLite/WAL database on unsupported network filesystems. #### 46.4.5. Failure scenarios and safe restoration Recovery procedures MUST distinguish missing original files; corrupted individual/global/both current JSONs; valid-but-semantically-wrong copies; disagreement; interrupted writes; disk exhaustion; moved/unavailable storage; external edits; multi-record AI mistakes; app disappearance; and missing decryption keys. Select and validate an evidenced recovery point, preserve recoverable damaged originals before potentially destructive restoration, and never overwrite the only surviving damaged source merely for convenience. Offer supported same-location or separately selected restoration destinations with understandable consequences; use isolated validation where appropriate. Verify restored bytes, metadata, relationships, IDs and declared recovery point before adoption. Restored paths and symlinks MUST NOT escape the selected destination or overwrite unrelated/unapproved files. Detect absolute-path/traversal escapes, reserved names, case/Unicode collisions and target permission differences; preserve original names and required unsupported metadata through documented reversible mappings or report the unsupported restoration, rather than silently merging distinct files. Apply safe path confinement, symlink/traversal handling, collision/name mapping and current authorization under [IO-1](#io-1), [PORT-2](#port-2) and [RECOVER-1](#recover-1). If no surviving authorized source/key/dependency supports recovery, report the limitation without invented data or false guarantees.

metadata.applies: saving, synchronization, conflict resolution, and restoration of retained-data workspaces

REV-1.title: Git-inspired content and revision evidence
REV-1.body: ### 47.1. REV-1 — Git-inspired content and revision evidence **Type:** ECOSYSTEM POLICY | **Origin:** USER POLICY | **Applies:** retained-data workspace change tracking and external modification reconciliation #### 47.1.1. Revision and change evidence Use stable revision identities, cryptographic content hashes, content comparisons, change manifests, structured differences where meaningful, recorded timestamps and previous-version relationships, content provenance and links to protected immutable verified history. Evaluate chunk-level hashing where useful for large content. Relevant change records MUST capture record identity, previous/new revision, affected fields/files, measured change size, recorded time and temporal context, old/new hashes, authorized operation identity where established, outcome, historical-content relationships and validation status where applicable. Unknown actors or times remain unknown; [DATA-5](#data-5), [AUDIT-1](#audit-1) and [EVID-1](#evid-1) govern evidence and retention. #### 47.1.2. What hashes establish Hashes identify/compare bytes against expected values; they neither store recoverable payloads nor prove authorship, time, legitimacy or factual correctness. Hashes/diffs MUST supplement, not replace, complete JSON payloads. Integrity against malicious rewriting requires the protected references/threat assumptions of [AUDIT-3](#audit-3). #### 47.1.3. External changes and detection latency External changes by editors, other programs, AI filesystem writes, cloud sync or NAS clients MUST be promptly flagged where supported. Define expected identities/revisions, watcher monitoring where available, hash/version verification, rescan/reconciliation and clear user-visible discrepancies. Watchers may miss events; the application may be stopped; remote changes may not yet have propagated. Mandatory integrity reconciliation at relevant trust/commit boundaries MUST precede destructive overwrite or authoritative adoption, coupled to transitions under [CON-1](#con-1); do not promise instantaneous detection everywhere. #### 47.1.4. Legitimate edits and safe adoption An external edit is not automatically malicious. Preserve its version within legitimate retention/privacy limits, compare with verified state, and provide safe authorized adoption, rejection or preserved alternatives. An older JSON MUST NOT silently overwrite the user's changed original, and unvalidated external bytes MUST NOT blindly propagate into both JSON layers. Report unresolved conflicts and containment through [EDIT-1](#edit-1), [EDIT-2](#edit-2) and [SYNC-1](#sync-1).

REV-2.title: Protected earlier revisions beyond current duplication
REV-2.body: ### 47.2. REV-2 — Protected earlier revisions beyond current duplication **Type:** ECOSYSTEM POLICY | **Origin:** USER POLICY | **Applies:** historical recovery protection for retained-user-data workspaces #### 47.2.1. Independent historical recovery points Provide independently protected historical recovery points in addition to the two current JSON layers. Equal current copies cannot undo an incorrect change already propagated to both. The design MUST address AI mistakes, deletion, incorrect transcript/user edits, corrupted JSON, synchronization errors, malicious changes, overwrites and storage failures, with declared failure domains, retention and platform capabilities. #### 47.2.2. Deletion authority and finite retention Normal application and AI editing credentials SHOULD NOT automatically have unrestricted deletion authority over every protected backup generation. Define meaningful separation of normal mutation and historical deletion authority, protected content/revision verification, recovery dependencies and actual residual risk under [BACKUP-1](#backup-1). Immutable verified history means protected recorded revisions under the declared threat/retention model, not perpetual retention, proof of factual correctness or immunity to root compromise. Authorized erasure/expiry remains enforceable under [PRIV-1](#priv-1), including prevention of forbidden resurrection. Finite snapshot scope follows [JSON-3](#json-3). No recovery guarantee survives destruction of all independent copies, required keys and dependencies.

metadata.applies: historical recovery protection for retained-user-data workspaces

WORKSPACE-1.title: Independently accessible durable workspace
WORKSPACE-1.body: ### 45.1. WORKSPACE-1 — Independently accessible durable workspace **Type:** ECOSYSTEM POLICY | **Origin:** USER POLICY | **Applies:** applications retaining user-owned information #### 45.1.1. Independent access and physical adaptation The App Plan MUST define one logical, discoverable, documented, independently accessible user-owned data workspace, separate from disposable application installation state. It SHOULD use a real user-accessible folder structure wherever the supported platform permits it. A technically necessary physical adaptation MUST document its mapping and preserve independent discovery, access and recovery outcomes; hidden opaque storage is not an equivalent substitute. Ordinary original documents/media and human-readable files MUST remain present and independently accessible within the supported storage/security contract. SQLite and other operational stores MAY serve appropriate responsibilities but MUST NOT replace [JSON-1](#json-1)'s recovery representations. #### 45.1.2. Planning priorities and platform survival Planning MUST prioritize human comprehension, information preservation, independent recovery, clear folder relationships, deterministic machine navigation, safe AI operations, scalability, and long-term compatibility. Document access without the original application, schemas/readers, retention and key dependencies under [SURVIVE-1](#survive-1)–[SURVIVE-2](#survive-2). An independently preserved recovery representation must actually survive the declared application-disappearance scenario; exposing app-private files through a picker or calling them external does not establish survival. Supported phone/provider access, permission persistence, offline availability and uninstall behavior MUST be researched and validated; arbitrary permanent filesystem access MUST NOT be promised for every phone or cloud service.

metadata.applies: applications retaining user-owned information

WORKSPACE-2.title: Selected location, identity, movement, and reconnection
WORKSPACE-2.body: ### 45.2. WORKSPACE-2 — Selected location, identity, movement, and reconnection **Type:** ECOSYSTEM POLICY | **Origin:** USER POLICY | **Applies:** setup and lifecycle of retained-user-data workspaces #### 45.2.1. Setup and stable identity Every applicable App Plan MUST identify where actual data lives. First setup SHOULD ask the user to select or approve a persistent workspace location: a suitable local folder or another supported storage arrangement. Remember the approved location and stable workspace identity, and use it until a deliberate authorized change. The application MUST NOT silently change authoritative location or create a replacement empty workspace when the configured location is unavailable. #### 45.2.2. Missing location and damaged information For an unavailable configured location, report **“Data location not found.”** Provide understandable reconnection steps and verify the candidate workspace's stable identity and contents before adoption. Distinguish missing/unreachable location, revoked permission, and damaged information; diagnostics must not claim corruption merely because access failed. For detected damage, report **“Data integrity issue detected.”** and offer verified recovery under [JSON-4](#json-4). #### 45.2.3. Verified movement and rebinding Movement between folders, drives, devices, NAS, and supported cloud arrangements MUST have documented and verified migration/reconnection procedures. Prefer relative internal references with an explicit base; stable record identities MUST survive physical folder/name changes. Rebind host-specific paths deliberately, verify permissions/schema/identity/contents and reconcile pending/concurrent changes before adopting a relocated workspace. Document rollback and incomplete movement without silently declaring success. Respect [PORT-2](#port-2), [MIGRATE-1](#migrate-1), and [SYNC-4](#sync-4).

metadata.applies: setup and lifecycle of retained-user-data workspaces

WORKSPACE-3.title: Three architectures and meaningful folder contracts
WORKSPACE-3.body: ### 45.3. WORKSPACE-3 — Three architectures and meaningful folder contracts **Type:** ECOSYSTEM POLICY | **Origin:** USER POLICY | **Applies:** substantial application planning, with workspace detail required for persistent-data applications #### 45.3.1. Workspace, planning, and implementation responsibilities Planning MUST separately assess and validate **A: User Data Workspace**, **B: Master Plan**, and **C: Codebase**, including cross-references and distinct ownership/responsibilities. If no user information is retained, document A as inapplicable. Master Plan retains [BLUEPRINT-1](#blueprint-1)'s Languages and Data, complete specification, Research and Decisions, Design, Reviews, Project State and sequential phases/subphases. Codebase retains feature-first frontend, backend, database and genuine shared responsibilities. `Codebase/Database/` schemas/migrations are development artifacts, not actual user data by default. #### 45.3.2. Per-folder and per-file design contract For substantial persistent-data applications, the data hierarchy MUST be explicitly designed, explained, challenged and validated before plan approval. An attractive tree alone is insufficient. Use extensive meaningful headings/subheadings without arbitrary heading limits. Each meaningful folder/file or documented homogeneous class MUST establish purpose, ownership, contents, format, naming, relationships, dependencies, authority/replica/projection/historical-evidence role, rebuildability, discovery, human reading, AI reading, permitted modification, change detection, corruption detection, recovery, relocation behavior, access controls, and retention. Class-level contracts must resolve every actual member's role; they cannot hide exceptional authoritative content. Do not create customary or empty folders without a demonstrated responsibility. Validate the hierarchy through [WORKSPACE-TEST-1](#workspace-test-1), and keep the complete intended specification and its technical records consistent under [BLUEPRINT-2](#blueprint-2).

WORKSPACE-4.title: Human and machine entry documents
WORKSPACE-4.body: ### 45.4. WORKSPACE-4 — Human and machine entry documents **Type:** ECOSYSTEM POLICY | **Origin:** USER POLICY | **Applies:** substantial retained-data workspaces and their independent discovery/recovery interfaces #### 45.4.1. Five discoverable entry responsibilities The preferred human-facing filesystem entry pattern is the following four primary information documents plus the complete global recovery representation. A technically necessary physical adaptation MUST explicitly map each responsibility and retain the same user-facing discovery and recovery outcome; it cannot omit the literal JSON obligation. | Entry | Required responsibility | |---|---| | `00-START-HERE.md` | Plain-English, non-programmer guidance: what this workspace contains, where to begin, major folders, finding information, and recovery when the original application no longer exists. | | `01-FOLDER-GUIDE.md` | Complete directory architecture, purposes, relationships, identity/navigation conventions and concrete examples; link each meaningful folder/file contract. | | `02-DATA-DICTIONARY.md` | Actual formats, fields, relationships, IDs, provenance, timestamp meaning, schema/revision versions, encodings and recovery concepts/dependencies. | | `catalog.json` | Validated navigable catalog resolving stable records to current logical locations through bounded machine retrieval; explicit authority, update/consistency policy, validation and reconstruction procedure. | | `master-data.json` | One complete literal global JSON recovery representation under [JSON-1](#json-1), not a hash list or pointer catalog. | #### 45.4.2. Independent bootstrap and protected discovery Documentation and recovery schemas MUST remain obtainable and usable without the original application or AI Skill. Catalog reconstruction and recovery discovery MUST not depend circularly on an intact catalog or global JSON: document bootstrap procedures using surviving individual records, protected history or independent recovery dependencies as appropriate. Routine AI retrieval uses bounded catalog/index interfaces, not full scans; authorized deterministic reconstruction may scan with declared costs. Private metadata and credentials remain protected under [AUTH-1](#auth-1), [PRIV-1](#priv-1) and [SEC-2](#sec-2).

metadata.applies: substantial retained-data workspaces and their independent discovery/recovery interfaces

WORKSPACE-AI-1.title: One discoverable primary application Skill
WORKSPACE-AI-1.body: ### 48.1. WORKSPACE-AI-1 — One discoverable primary application Skill **Type:** ECOSYSTEM POLICY | **Origin:** USER POLICY | **Applies:** AI-accessible applications with retained-user-data workspaces #### 48.1.1. Primary Skill navigation and operation contract Expose one clearly named discoverable primary trusted application Skill, for example `Menemora/SKILL.md`. It MUST explain application purpose, approved workspace location/discovery, entry point, folders, record discovery, bounded retrieval, schema/revision interpretation, edit requests, source-data versus instruction boundaries, approval requirements, enforced permissions, error/ambiguity handling, change verification, objects never directly modified, and reporting of uncertain/blocked outcomes. It MAY route to justified bounded subordinate Skills/documentation; one primary entry does not prohibit specialized expertise. #### 48.1.2. Trusted registration and enforced permissions Trust and invocation MUST follow [SKILL-1](#skill-1)–[SKILL-3](#skill-3). An editable workspace file, including a file named SKILL.md, cannot authenticate itself or elevate authority. Trusted registration/revision and enforced permission boundaries remain separate from its text. AI application operations MUST use approved permission-enforced application interfaces; the Skill alone grants no direct filesystem mutation, credential access, deletion, production or other elevated authority. Existing separately delegated coding/scratch capabilities remain scoped under [AI-1](#ai-1) and do not bypass runtime data protections. Human workspace documentation MUST remain usable without the Skill.

metadata.applies: AI-accessible applications with retained-user-data workspaces

WORKSPACE-AI-2.title: Measurable one-billion-parameter navigation target
WORKSPACE-AI-2.body: ### 48.2. WORKSPACE-AI-2 — Measurable one-billion-parameter navigation target **Type:** ECOSYSTEM POLICY | **Origin:** USER POLICY | **Applies:** AI workspace navigation design and material small-model capability claims #### 48.2.1. Bounded retrieval route Design for appropriately scoped data navigation by a suitably capable model around **1 billion parameters**. The preferred route is **AI → trusted application Skill → 00-START-HERE.md → folder guide and catalog → bounded retrieval operation → relevant record and precise content**. Supply clear entry points, stable IDs, readable names, bounded indexes/catalogs, precise sub-object addresses, deterministic lookup, limited outputs, ambiguity reporting, enforced authorization, task-specific examples and documented errors. A model MUST NOT need to read the complete global JSON, massive database or thousands of files merely to retrieve one ordinary record. #### 48.2.2. Actual evaluation and separate development target Material capability claims MUST identify model/version and available parameter/quantization evidence, environment/tools/context limits, representative tasks and actual evaluation. Measure retrieval accuracy, errors, hallucinated paths, unauthorized mutations, context budget and correct escalation. Record passed/failed/unrun results and limits; parameter count alone proves no capability. Preserve [HERMES-2](#hermes-2)'s local constrained-model testing and [EXEC-6](#exec-6)'s separate approximately 4B code-execution target. Navigating data and implementing an application are distinct evaluations.

metadata.applies: AI workspace navigation design and material small-model capability claims

WORKSPACE-TEST-1.title: Navigation, restoration, and aggressive failure trials
WORKSPACE-TEST-1.body: ### 49.1. WORKSPACE-TEST-1 — Navigation, restoration, and aggressive failure trials **Type:** ECOSYSTEM POLICY | **Origin:** USER POLICY | **Applies:** design and implementation verification of retained-data workspaces #### 49.1.1. Design simulations and implemented scenarios Plans MUST simulate, then implementations MUST verify representative scenarios: human and small-AI record location; understanding folders without the app; moving the entire workspace; restoring a deleted original; corrupt individual JSON; corrupt global JSON; external modification detection; application-disappearance recovery; large-dataset navigation; interrupted/conflicting NAS/cloud changes; and restoration to another selected location. Mark design-time simulation separately from actual implementation testing; a plan is not demonstrated recovery. #### 49.1.2. Failure battery and acceptance criteria Define demanding documented acceptance criteria and appropriate fault injection, crashes, disk-full conditions, malformed/truncated JSON, missing originals, concurrent writes, interrupted commits, power-loss assumptions, NAS/cloud disconnection, remote conflicts, destructive AI mistakes, large media, lifetime-scale datasets, failed migrations, app-disappearance recovery, small-model navigation, memory/CPU, startup/search performance, and backup/restore checks. Include valid-but-wrong JSON and propagated mistakes, not only parse failures. Verify authorization, privacy/deletion, keys, recovery-point truth and no-fallback boundaries alongside successful reconstruction. #### 49.1.3. Isolated fixtures and finite repair Use isolated fixtures and authorized test environments; never deliberately damage live user data. Test, repair, retest and repeat until the documented quality baseline is met or a material unresolved limitation is accurately reported. A compilation or happy-path demo alone is insufficient. Testing is finite and risk-based, with actual outcomes under [TEST-1](#test-1); it does not prove absence of all future defects or waive [EXEC-3](#exec-3)'s bounded repair/escalation contract.

metadata.applies: design and implementation verification of retained-data workspaces

WORKSPACE-TEST-2.title: Literal JSON capacity and feasible workload
WORKSPACE-TEST-2.body: ### 49.2. WORKSPACE-TEST-2 — Literal JSON capacity and feasible workload **Type:** ECOSYSTEM POLICY | **Origin:** USER POLICY | **Applies:** workload planning and performance claims for literal dual-JSON storage #### 49.2.1. Workload and lifetime costs Evaluate capacity, storage amplification, temporary write space, write frequency, serialization time, crash consistency, memory, backup growth, cloud upload/transfer cost, NAS bandwidth, mobile constraints, concurrent access and lifetime growth under [DEV-16](#dev-16). State assumptions and measured or estimated evidence, including workload and target-platform limits. A small edit may require producing a new complete global JSON representation; hashing alone cannot remove the payload requirement. #### 49.2.2. Logical storage amplification For illustration, 100 GB of binary originals plus approximately 133 GB of Base64 payloads in individual JSON and 133 GB in global JSON totals about **366 GB** before other overhead, temporary generations and history. This is approximate logical storage accounting, not a measured universal physical requirement. For binary lengths nᵢ, N = Σnᵢ and B = Σ(4 × ceil(nᵢ/3)), originals plus two single-encoded layers require approximately N + 2B; for large inputs this approaches 11N/3, so 100 decimal GB is approximately 366.7 GB. The rounded 366 GB illustration assumes each layer encodes each original payload once. Encoding an already encoded individual JSON envelope again inside the global layer adds expansion; separately encoded chunks add padding/framing. The actual schema must account for these costs rather than assume this estimate universally. Git uses separately stored content objects and references, unlike one literal complete JSON payload. #### 49.2.3. Peak resources and streaming limits Memory estimates MUST include the largest parser/encoder token and buffers: streaming records does not bound memory if an enormous Base64 string is allocated at once. Measure or bound peak disk while prior valid state and staging coexist, total bytes written/transferred, CPU, latency and growth; bounded memory does not remove total serialization, validation or I/O costs. #### 49.2.4. Measured optimizations and material conflicts Streaming serialization, compression, copy-on-write, snapshots, sparse files, reflinks and other optimizations MAY be evaluated within the eventual approved design, but their portability, actual savings, crash behavior and recovery dependencies require evidence. None is universally selected here or excuses complete payloads. If literal duplication cannot meet the agreed workload, present the material conflict honestly to the owner and resolve affected planning under [GOV-3](#gov-3) and [DEV-5](#dev-5); do not silently replace payloads with pointers, invent capacity, hide loss or implement a fallback.

metadata.applies: workload planning and performance claims for literal dual-JSON storage
